# Schur-corrected central-pair curvature of simplex capacities

This note proves positive optimized-capacity curvature in a corrected pair direction. It does not identify that direction with the original pair direction, and does not assert a universal capacity Hessian signature. The conclusion holds in every dimension d>=2 for a full row with a proper minimizing threshold. Threshold nondegeneracy is proved below, including repeated entries and cuts through vertices.

For a uniform barycentric vector U on the d-simplex, let

    F_x(t)=Pr(x dot U<=t),
    phi_d(x)=inf_(t>0,F_x(t)>0) t/F_x(t)^(1/d).

A full row x has every coordinate positive. A proper threshold lies strictly between its smallest and largest entries. The source `candidate 78b95c208ba2d374` proves that a full nonconstant row has a unique minimizing threshold; when proper, its capacity is differentiable and its actual section centroid b gives the envelope gradient. The source `candidate 8704554a92158bfc`, Sections 1–4, proves the reciprocal-transform Hessian lemma used below. Neither source asserts the Schur correction proved here.

## 1. Joint second derivatives, including zero margins

Let c have at least two positive coordinates and at least one negative coordinate. Then

    P(c)=Pr(sum c_j E_j>=0),

for independent unit exponentials E_j, is jointly C2 in a neighborhood of c. Repeated nonzero coordinates and zero coordinates are allowed.

Here are details for the regularity needed in this note. Select two positive coefficients a,b and one negative coefficient -r, all bounded away from zero in a neighborhood. For W=aE_1+bE_2-rE_3, its survival function is

    S(w)=1-exp(w/r) r^2/[(a+r)(b+r)]                 (w<=0),
    S(w)=[a^2 exp(-w/a)/(a+r)
          -b^2 exp(-w/b)/(b+r)]/(a-b)               (w>=0).

At a=b the second formula is its divided-difference limit. That limit is smooth in positive a,b, for example by the integral representation of a first divided difference. The two expressions and their first two w derivatives agree at w=0. These identities remain true after parameter differentiation, so S is jointly C2 in (w,a,b,r). Its derivatives through order two are bounded uniformly in w and in a compact positive parameter neighborhood; this follows directly from the displayed exponential formulas and their divided-difference integral.

Condition on all remaining exponentials. Their linear combination Y may include coefficients of either sign or zero. Then P(c)=E[S(-Y)]. Differentiation through order two is dominated by a fixed constant times (1+sum E_j)^2. This integrable bound proves the asserted joint C2 property and continuity of those derivatives.

Put g=grad P(c), H=Hess P(c). The probability is homogeneous of degree zero, hence

    g dot c=0,       Hc=-g.                          (1)

The section-centroid identity is

    g_j=d f_V(0)b_j,
    sum_j g_j=d f_V(0),                              (2)

where V=sum c_jE_j. These formulas follow either from exponential size bias or from the first variation of the actual simplex section. Every g_j is positive at a proper cut.

## 2. Exact threshold Schur complement

Scale a full row and its proper minimizing threshold simultaneously so that the threshold is 1. Set c=1-x, P=P(c), and

    eta=H 1,       u=1^T H 1,
    B=d(d-1)P-u,   K=P^(-1/d)/(dP).

Threshold stationarity of L(x,t)=t P(t1-x)^(-1/d) gives

    1^Tg=dP.                                        (3)

In particular f_V(0)=P and g_j/P=d b_j. Direct differentiation, before reoptimizing t, gives at t=1

    L_xx=K[(d+1)gg^T/(dP)-H],
    L_xt=K(eta-dg),
    L_tt=KB.                                        (4)

Suppose B>0. The implicit-function theorem gives a C1 minimizing-threshold function nearby. Uniqueness at x and compact localization of nearby minimizing thresholds rule out a remote minimizer switch; thus this local branch is the actual minimum. The optimized capacity is C2 and

    Hess phi_d
      =K[(d+1)gg^T/(dP)-H
                -(eta-dg)(eta-dg)^T/B].             (5)

This is the Schur term that cannot be omitted.

Let v satisfy g dot v=0, and define

    w=v+(eta dot v)/(dP) 1.                          (6)

Equation (5) gives exactly

    v^T Hess(phi_d)v=K[-v^THv-(eta dot v)^2/B],
    v^T Hess(phi_d)1=K dP(eta dot v)/B,
    1^T Hess(phi_d)1=-K d^2P^2/B.

Substituting (6) cancels the three B-dependent terms:

    w^T Hess(phi_d)w=-K v^THv.                       (7)

Thus a negative cap-probability Hessian direction tangent to g becomes a positive optimized-capacity direction after the explicit common shift. No sign is asserted for the uncorrected direction v.

## 3. A central captured pair supplies the negative cap direction

Choose two strictly positive margins c_i,c_j and assume their actual section-centroid coordinates satisfy b_i,b_j<=1/d. Put

    q_i=g_i/P=d b_i, q_j=g_j/P=d b_j,
    v_i=q_j, v_j=-q_i, v_l=0 otherwise.

Then g dot v=0. For completeness, the exact input from the cited stationary-cap source is as follows. Hold the current density f_V fixed and set

    varphi(a)=f_(V+aE')(0)/f_V(0),   psi(a)=1/varphi(a).

The reciprocal Laplace-transform argument proves that psi is convex, psi(0+)=1, and psi'(a)>0 whenever psi(a)>=1. At a=c_i,c_j, varphi(a)=q_i,q_j<=1. Size bias gives

    v^THv=2P q_i^2q_j^2
       [D_ij psi-psi'(c_i)-psi'(c_j)]<0.             (8)

Here D_ij is the divided difference, or psi'(c_i) at equality. Convexity bounds the divided difference by the larger endpoint derivative, while the other derivative is strictly positive. This proves strict negativity even for repeated captured heights. The reciprocal-transform proof depends only on the two indicated central coordinates, not on centrality of all b.

Consequently, under B>0, equations (6)–(8) give an explicit direction of strictly positive optimized-capacity curvature in every dimension d>=2.

## 4. Every proper full-row threshold is nondegenerate, in all dimensions

The following mechanism was supplied by the the contributor and independently checked here. It removes the provisional B>0 premise from the geometric conclusion.

Normalize a full row's proper minimizing threshold to 1, so every positive coefficient of c=1-x is strictly less than 1. There is at least one negative coefficient by properness. There cannot be exactly one positive coefficient c_p. In that case, conditioning on Y=-sum_(c_j<0)c_jE_j gives

    P=E exp(-Y/c_p),       f_V(0)=P/c_p.

Threshold stationarity says P=f_V(0), hence c_p=1, contrary to x_p>0. Zero coefficients do not affect this argument. Therefore every proper minimizing cut of a full row has at least two positive and one negative coefficient. Section 1 gives joint C2 regularity.

The density f=f_V is positive, continuously differentiable, and log-concave on R. Positivity and C1 follow from the three-phase convolution in Section 1; log-concavity is the standard convolution consequence of Prekopa–Leindler for the signed exponential densities. As in the archived reciprocal-transform source, these are properties of the actual exponential sum, not assumptions on a sampled measure.

Write ell=f'(0)/f(0). Log-concavity gives the tangent bound

    f(s)<=f(0) exp(ell s),  s>=0.                     (9)

But integral_0^infinity f(s)ds=P=f(0). If ell<-1, integrating (9) gives P<f(0), impossible. If ell=-1, equality of the integrals and continuity force f(s)=f(0)exp(-s) for every s>=0.

This equality is also impossible. Since all positive c_j are less than 1, choose lambda>1 with lambda c_j<1 for each positive c_j. Independence gives

    E exp(lambda V)=product_j (1-lambda c_j)^(-1)<infinity.

(The factors for nonpositive c_j are harmless.) An exact positive exponential tail of rate 1 would make this moment infinite. Therefore

    f'(0)>-f(0)=-P.                                  (10)

For the sign relating this to B, let L=sum c_jU_j and G=sum E_j. The variables L and G are independent, V=GL, and G has gamma shape d+1. Since shifting all coefficients by s replaces L by L+s,

    u=1^TH1=-f_L'(0).

Also

    f_V'(0)=f_L'(0) E[G^(-2)]
            =f_L'(0)/[d(d-1)].                      (11)

Here is a boundary-safe justification of (11). The projection density f_L is bounded and compactly supported. Joint C2 in Section 1 makes f_L continuously differentiable on a neighborhood of zero, by the coefficient-shift identity. In

    f_V(v)=E[G^(-1)f_L(v/G)],

split at G=|v|/delta, with delta inside that neighborhood. The small-G contribution to the difference quotient is O(|v|^(d-1)), using boundedness of f_L and the gamma density O(G^d); it vanishes for d>=2. On the remaining part, the mean-value bound is a constant times G^(-2), integrable for d>=2. Dominated convergence proves (11). Boundedness of f_L follows directly from the coarea formula and bounded simplex sections.

Combining (10)–(11) gives the exact strict bound

    B=d(d-1)P-u=d(d-1)[P+f_V'(0)]>0.                (12)

Thus every full row with a proper minimizing threshold has a C2 optimized capacity in a neighborhood, and the Schur formula of Section 2 applies. The only uses of full positivity here are c_j<1 and compact positive-row threshold localization; no centrality is needed for nondegeneracy.

Consequently the central-pair conclusion of Section 3 is unconditional for all d>=2: whenever two strictly captured vertices have section-centroid coordinates at most 1/d, the optimized capacity has the explicit strictly positive direction (6).

## 4a. Independent tetrahedral face check

Let d=3, x be full, and let its minimizing threshold t be proper. At least two vertices are strictly captured. Indeed, if only one vertex has x_j<t, the cap is a vertex tetrahedron and

    F_x(t)^(1/3)=C(t-x_j)

up to and including the next vertex height. Since x_j>0, t/F_x(t)^(1/3) has strictly negative derivative there, including its left derivative at the next height; proper stationarity is impossible. There is at least one strictly excluded vertex. Thus Section 1 applies, including the possible margin pattern (+,+,-,0).

The root F_x^(1/3) is concave by Brunn–Minkowski for nested caps. At threshold stationarity, this implies L_tt>=0, hence B>=0 after normalizing t=1. Suppose B=0. In unnormalized variables this says

    t F_x'(t)=3F_x(t),
    t F_x''(t)=2F_x'(t).                             (13)

For the triangular face opposite vertex j, write F_j(t) for its captured area fraction. The elementary face-divergence identity is

    F_j(t)=F_x(t)+(x_j-t)F_x'(t)/3.                  (14)

It holds also at a vertex height by continuity. Differentiating is legitimate here: the tetrahedral CDF is C2 by Section 1, and every triangular-face CDF is C1 at a proper cut; full/empty face derivatives are interpreted by their actual one-sided formulas. Substitution of (13) yields

    F_j(t)=x_j F_x(t)/t>0,
    t F_j'(t)=2F_j(t)>0.                             (15)

If the tetrahedral cut strictly captures exactly two vertices, delete one captured vertex. The remaining triangle has exactly one strictly captured vertex, say l, with any boundary vertices permitted. Its cap formula up to this threshold is

    F_j(t)=C(t-x_l)^2,

so t F_j'(t)-2F_j(t)=2C x_l(t-x_l)>0, contradicting (15). The formula and first derivative remain valid when one other vertex lies exactly on the cut.

If the tetrahedral cut strictly captures three vertices, delete its sole excluded vertex. That face is fully captured in a neighborhood, so F_j'=0, again contradicting (15).

These exhaust the possible proper minimizing cuts with at least two strictly captured vertices. Therefore B>0. In particular every full tetrahedral row with a proper minimizing cut has a C2 capacity near that row, including cuts through one vertex and repeated entries on either strict side.

Combining this fact with Section 3 proves the unconditional tetrahedral conclusion: if two strictly captured vertices have section-centroid coordinates at most 1/3, the optimized capacity has a strictly positive Hessian direction given by (6).

## 5. Exact rank consequence and its limit

For a column-stochastic matrix, the all-ones vector belongs to the span of its active rows, because their sum equals that vector. Therefore if the pair vector v above belongs to that span, its corrected vector w also belongs to the span. The projective-variation lemma in `candidate f62fe2e83b180bf3` then excludes this full row at a positive-weight maximum.

In particular, in dimension d an attained positive-weight maximum with d+1 linearly independent active rows cannot have a full row whose proper minimizing section captures two coordinates at most 1/d. Membership of the pair vector in a rank-three active span is a separate condition; it is not established here. Nor does this note establish that every full row in a given matrix has such a pair. Those are geometric compatibility questions about the several rows, not consequences of the Schur calculation.

Uniqueness alone was not used to infer nondegeneracy. Section 4 proves it through an actual log-concave exponential density and a finite exponential moment; no strict Brunn–Minkowski differential equality claim is needed.

## 6. Noncentral section coordinates lie on one side

For any proper section whose exponential sum has a positive C1 log-concave density f, every barycentric section-centroid coordinate greater than 1/d belongs to the same strict side of the section. In particular this applies to all proper minimizing sections of full rows by Section 4.

Here is a short proof not requiring a limiting derivative of the reciprocal transform. Put ell=f'(0)/f(0). For a strictly positive margin c_j, size bias gives

    d b_j=g_j/f(0)
          =integral_0^infinity exp(-s) f(-c_j s)/f(0) ds.

If ell>=0, the log-concave tangent bound gives f(-c_j s)<=f(0)exp(-ell c_j s)<=f(0), and hence d b_j<=1. Thus a noncentral coordinate on the positive side forces ell<0. Applying the same argument to -V, a noncentral coordinate on the negative side forces ell>0. Both conditions cannot hold. A zero margin has g_j=f(0), hence b_j=1/d, and cannot be noncentral. This proves the assertion with all boundary signs tracked.

As an immediate consequence, a positive-weight stochastic capacity maximum with d+1 linearly independent full rows is impossible. Indeed the full-cut exclusion in the cited positive-row regularity source makes every row's minimizing cut proper (a full matrix has all entries less than 1). Feasible column transfers give identical weighted gradients of all rows. By their gradient formula, all actual section-centroid vectors equal one common positive vector b. Let t_i=x_i dot b be their thresholds; summing column-stochastic rows gives sum_i t_i=1, so their raw margins c_ij=t_i-x_ij satisfy

    sum_i c_ij=0 for every column j.                 (16)

If b has no coordinate greater than 1/d, every row captures at least two central coordinates. If it has such a coordinate j, that coordinate has nonzero margin in every row by the preceding lemma. Equation (16) forces some row to have c_ij<0. In that row all noncentral coordinates lie on its negative side, so every captured coordinate is central; there are at least two captured coordinates. The strictly positive curvature direction of Sections 2–4 therefore exists. Full row rank places that direction in the active-row span, and the exact projective-variation lemma contradicts maximality.

In particular a least-active maximizing representative cannot consist of d+1 full rows, because its active rows are independent. This statement does not classify representatives with fewer full rows or mixtures of full and one-zero rows.
